editorial:
You follow Julie, a young woman in Oslo who keeps changing her mind about love, work, and who she wants to be. Over four years, she moves between relationships and jobs, trying to figure out what actually makes her happy. The film feels warm, funny, and honest, with a loose, lived-in rhythm that makes her messy choices feel real instead of judged. It is less about big drama and more about the small, awkward moments that shape a life.

Renate Reinsve gives a bright, natural performance, and the supporting cast keeps every scene grounded. The pacing is relaxed but never boring, with sharp humor and quiet emotional turns. Some viewers may want a bigger plot, but the small moments are the point.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Julie has ended things with Eivind and is living on her own after years of searching for the right path. Aksel has died, and Julie processes grief while accepting that she cannot control every part of life. The closing moments show her moving forward with quiet hope, not a neat happy ending, but a real sense that she is finally becoming herself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven romance and honest coming-of-age stories.
